{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping the row with the highest sample_seq
# First, ensure sample_seq is numeric
data['sample_seq'] = pd.to_numeric(data['sample_seq'], errors='coerce')

# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending) to ensure highest sample_seq comes first
data_sorted = data.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Drop duplicates on patient_id, keeping the first (highest sample_seq)
deduplicated_data = data_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Check that we now have one row per patient
n_patients = deduplicated_data['patient_id'].nunique()
print(f'Number of unique patients after deduplication: {n_patients}')

# Now, handle the assay_batch issue: batch B reports in µg/L, not ng/mL
# 1 µg/L = 10 ng/mL, so batch B values are 10× too large
# So we divide batch B values by 10
# Create a copy to avoid modifying the original
result_data = deduplicated_data.copy()
result_data.loc[result_data['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_final'] = result_data.loc[result_data['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_final'] / 10

# Now compute the mean of biomarker_final in ng/mL
mean_biomarker_final = result_data['biomarker_final'].mean()
print(f'Mean biomarker_final (ng/mL) across all patients: {mean_biomarker_final}')"}
